## Extraction notes

*What the schema could not express about this repository. This is the
part of a record worth reading: field values say what fits, these say
what does not — and they are the input to any schema proposal.*

**14 notes.**

### 1.

Notebook locators. The schema's evidence format is `path:lines`, which is unusable for .ipynb files — a raw JSON line number points at an escaped string, not at code a reader can find. All notebook evidence in this record uses `path:cellN` with N the zero-based index into the `cells` array. The schema should state a notebook locator convention; p01's artifacts apparently did not force the question.

### 2.

The generator, the system under test and the judge are all the same model, and the schema cannot say so. models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite writes the 997 questions (notebooks/ground_truth.ipynb:cell0), is one of the two answer generators under comparison (notebooks/rag.ipynb:cell16), and is the sole judge of both generators' relevance and faithfulness (notebooks/rag.ipynb:cell17,cell19) — including when it judges the rival model gemini-2.5-flash and loses to it. `llm_eval_judge_kind: model_judge` plus `llm_eval_question_generator: generator_ties_question_to_passage` capture two separate circularities but not the identity between the three roles, which is the stronger fact here. A field such as `llm_eval_judge_is_generator_model` (or a three-way `same`/`same_family`/`different`) would express it.

### 3.

Reported judge scores are computed over a filtered denominator, and no field records that. The judge functions return {verdict: None} on a JSON parse error (notebooks/rag.ipynb:cell17,cell19) and the reported figures come from `value_counts(normalize=True)`, which drops nulls. Counted in the committed artifacts: data/rag_results_for_eval_gemini-2.5-flash-lite.json has 76/997 null relevance and 35/997 null faithfulness; data/rag_results_for_eval_gemini-2.5-flash.json has 64/997 and 29/997. So README.md:181-182's '0.805 / 0.969' are rates over 921 and 962 items, not 997, and the README states no denominator. This is neither an untraceable number (the notebook does produce those digits) nor a document conflict; the schema has nowhere to put 'the reported metric silently excludes the items where measurement failed'. It is also the difference between a 96.9% faithfulness rate and a 93.5% one, so it is not cosmetic.

### 4.

The measured index and the shipped index are built from different sources by different code, and `retrieval_eval_config_matches_shipped` only half-fits. Every reported number was measured against a collection built in notebooks/rag.ipynb:cell2 from inspirehep.net using `id=int(hit['id'])`. Both committed ingestion scripts (src/ingest.py, src/ingest_json.py) build a collection of the same name from the arXiv API / a Kaggle snapshot using `uuid5` string ids and different payload keys. The retrieval metric's rule is `int(row['paper_id']) in retrieved_ids`, which cannot match a string uuid — so the evaluation is not merely measuring a differently-configured system, it is measuring an index no committed script can rebuild, and re-running the evaluation after following the README would report a hit rate of 0. README.md:12-25 names arXiv and Kaggle as the data sources and never mentions inspirehep.net. I set the field to `differs` on the schema's 'a pipeline stage present in one and not the other' clause, but every parameter the field explicitly lists (depth, cut-off, model version) matches, so a literal reading would return `matches`. The field's check should name the index/corpus provenance.

### 5.

The documentation names artifacts that do not exist, and the reachability fields are one-directional. README.md:202-228's project tree lists `src/ui.py` and `test.py`, neither of which is tracked (the Streamlit app is src/app.py; there is no test file), and names the three result files as `rag_results_eval_flash-lite.json`, `rag_results_eval_flash.json`, `rag_results_test.json` where the committed names are `rag_results_for_eval_gemini-2.5-flash-lite.json`, `rag_results_for_eval_gemini-2.5-flash.json`, `rag_results_for_test_eval.json`. `artifacts_unreferenced_count` measures artifacts nothing points at; there is no field for pointers that resolve to nothing, which is the same findability failure from the other end.

### 6.

`monitoring_chart_count` and `monitoring_charts_bound_to_data` assume a self-authored dashboard. Here monitoring is an off-the-shelf tracing UI (arizephoenix/phoenix:latest, docker-compose.yaml:38-47) that the application instruments with OpenTelemetry spans (src/rag.py:12-16,58-61,87-88; src/serve.py:8-14). The committed panel count is 0 and the binding check is not_applicable, yet the instrumentation is real and lives on the request path — so the two fields read as 'nothing here' for a project that did strictly more work than a project committing a Grafana JSON with three panels would. Something like `monitoring_instrumentation: none|logged|traced_on_request_path` would separate the two.

### 7.

`interface_kind` forces one value where this repository ships two interfaces. A FastAPI service (src/serve.py:47-58, published on 8080) and a Streamlit UI (src/app.py, published on 8501) are both built and run by docker-compose.yaml. I recorded `web_ui` as the higher rung of what looks like a tier ladder, but `api` is equally true and the record loses that. The field cannot distinguish 'web UI only' from 'API plus web UI'.

### 8.

`llm_eval_metric_at_ceiling` gives no threshold, so its value is not reproducible across extractors. Faithfulness is a binary verdict at 0.9688 and 0.9804 of parsed items; 'sits at its maximum for effectively every item' could be read either way at those values. I answered `false` because 30 and 19 items respectively do not take the maximum, and put the counts in `basis` — but a different extractor reading 'effectively' more loosely would answer `true` on the same evidence. The field needs a stated cutoff or should become a proportion.

### 9.

An evaluation's dependency is absent from the manifest, and `dependency_versions_pinned` cannot see it. The reranking comparison that README.md:166-170 rests on imports `sentence_transformers` (notebooks/rag.ipynb:cell10), which appears in neither pyproject.toml nor uv.lock. `dependency_versions_pinned: lockfile_committed` is the correct value and reads as the strongest available, while the environment the lockfile pins cannot execute the notebook that produced a reported result. Traceability of the *number* is intact only because the notebook outputs are stored.

### 10.

One question set serves both evaluations and nothing is held out. The same 997 rows of data/ground_truth_dataset.csv are used for the retrieval metrics (notebooks/rag.ipynb:cell7) and for generating and judging answers (cells 16, 17, 19, 24-26). The schema records set size and provenance but has no field for whether any portion was held out, or whether the retrieval and answer evaluations share items.

### 11.

`document_number_conflicts` is defined over 'figures', and the only conflict this repository offers is a port number (8000 in README.md:121,124 versus 8080 in README.md:134, docker-compose.yaml:26 and Dockerfile:23). I counted it as 1 and named it, but the field's surrounding prose is about headline metric figures, so an extractor reading it narrowly would answer 0. The conflict is also already counted as a gap under `run_instructions_gap_count`; the schema does not say whether the two fields are meant to overlap.

### 12.

One gap in `run_instructions_gap_count` rests on library semantics rather than on the repository alone: gap (4), `dtype={'id', str}` passed to pandas.read_json. Knowing that a set is neither a bool nor a mapping is Python knowledge, not domain knowledge, so I judged it admissible under the schema's rule 1, but it is the one gap a reader cannot confirm from the repository text by itself. Gap (1), bash `echo` not interpreting `\n` without `-e`, is of the same character and is noted for the same reason.

### 13.

No file path in this repository contains a person's name; no anonymity exception was needed.

### 14.

Domain knowledge was not required for any field. The corpus is English throughout, so the schema's rule-1 stress test (p02 being noted as domain-opaque) did not bind here in the way expected: the subject matter is specialised, but every field was answerable by counting rows, comparing code paths and reading stored notebook outputs.
